assets.statement: Parity lemma refuted by Kummer: k&(n−k)=0 gives odd C(n,k); (7,3)=35 with lpf 5>7/2, and infinitely many (2^m−1,k) instances; branch-A close must instead bound small prime factors of odd coefficients directly.

L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.

L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

standing lemmas cover only squarefree-supported subfamily + finite witness set, violating canonical quantifier "for every n" (subsequence/domain-drift kill); repair: uniform exponent function on full powerful-number domain, all mixed prime-power supports, tail f(n)≤n^{e(n)} for every sufficiently la

f(1+p+q)=pq refuted: n=15=1+3+11 has f(15)=8 (m=8: 1+2+4+8)<33 and n=25=1+11+13 has f(25)=36 (m=36: 1+2+3+4+6+9)<143; the canonical witness is not the minimizer, so balanced Goldbach yields only an upper bound and cannot close part (iii).
witness (n,k)=(7,3): C(7,3)=35, lpf=5 > max(7/3,3)=3, refuting the strict ∀-form; canonical statement survives only via its finitely-many-exceptions clause, so branch B cannot close on L1 alone.
